key_insight: Explainable machine learning can pinpoint where household WASH inequities are greatest in Nigeria, highlighting low-wealth rural northern households as the highest-priority group for intervention.
clinical_relevance: Better targeting of WASH resources may strengthen neglected tropical disease prevention by focusing support on the populations most likely to have inadequate water and sanitation access.
method: Cross-sectional secondary analysis of 30,045 households from the 2024 Nigeria DHS
Compared Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and XGBoost to predict improved household WASH access
Used SHAP values and feature importance to explain the strongest predictors
evidence_signal: XGBoost performed best with 83.3% accuracy and 0.877 AUC, while Random Forest was close behind with 0.868 AUC.
watch_item: Because this is a cross-sectional observational analysis, the models identify associations rather than causal effects, so deployment should be validated before guiding resource allocation.
paper_title: Predicting and Explaining WASH Inequities in Nigeria A Machine Learning Approach to Accelerate NTD Elimination
